findings.issue: Test-isolation hazard created by the new unconditional sanitization block, not covered by the Edge cases. migrateData(null) returns { ...DEFAULT_DATA, boards: [{ ...DEFAULT_DATA.boards[0] }] } — a shallow spread, so the returned board's `groups` object IS DEFAULT_DATA.boards[0].groups (the task acknowledges this sharing but scopes it out). The new sanitization block writes group.title for every group of every board, so any test that feeds a default-derived object back through migrateData (the retargeted idempotency test does exactly that) writes into the module-level DEFAULT_DATA. With valid data the write is value-identical and harmless, but a TDD-Anchor case that seeds a damaged title onto a board obtained from migrateData(null) would corrupt DEFAULT_DATA for every later test in the file, in test-declaration order.
findings.fix: Add a one-line note to the TDD Anchor: build damaged-title / damaged-order fixtures with the existing makeBoard() helper, never by mutating the result of migrateData(null); reserve migrateData(null) for the idempotency and fresh-array assertions.

findings.issue: Step 4 says the name input's 'value is the raw stored title — board.groups[groupId].title as it sits in data.json'. Read literally that is a bind to the `board` prop, which is the same object instance held by dataStore — binding to it would mutate the store on every keystroke and silently break the AC 'Cancel and an overlay click discard both'. Step 1 and the Implementation hints do say the value lives in local `groupTitles` seeded verbatim from board.groups[id].title (?? ''), so the intent is right; only step 4's wording is ambiguous, and it is the step an implementer reads while writing the markup.
findings.fix: Reword step 4 to 'bind the input to groupTitles[groupId] (seeded verbatim from board.groups[groupId].title, ?? "") — never bind to the board prop'.
